newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-YOUNGEST WALKER CUP PLAYER IN HISTORY.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-YOUNGEST WALKER CUP PLAYER IN HISTORY.

text.p: The Britain and Ireland team have picked the youngest player ever selected for the Walker Cup for this year's biennial amateur team match against the United States in August.
Justin Rose will be just 10 days past his 17th birthday when the 36th match is played at Quaker Ridge, New York, on August 9 and 10.
The previous youngest was Ronan Rafferty, who played in 1981 when he was 17 years seven months.
Rose was born in South Africa but moved with his family to England when he was five.
He has won many junior events, including the under-18 English strokeplay title when he was just 14, and recently captured his first senior title, the St Andrews Links Trophy.

Rose is one of only two Englishman on the team. The other is Gary Wolstenholme, 20 years Rose's senior, who famously defeated the now-world number one Tiger Woods when Britain and Ireland won at Royal Porthcawl two years ago.
Scotland provide five of the team, Ireland two and Wales one.
